summary: LTP subscriptions on two equities: an LTP packet becomes an LTP frame with its trade time in epoch ms; a binary frame carrying two packets back to back serves both instruments, where the web decodes only the first.

notes: The query carries x_jwt_token (paytm_websocket.py:232); subscriptions are JSON arrays of preferences.

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; the Paytm web adapter puts its subscription mode number there.

The web passes Paytm's trade time on in epoch seconds; WebSocket times are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md, CLAUDE.md), so a client reading ltt as ms on the web lands in January 1970. The desktop sends milliseconds.
deviations.ref: paytm_adapter.py:702, 709, 728 (raw last_traded_time); audit remaining brokers matrix (Paytm: native seconds -> ms)

deviations.reason: The web's client decodes only the first packet of a binary frame (paytm_websocket.py:101-108, _parse_binary_data reads byte 0's packet), so a second packet in the same frame is lost; the desktop cuts every packet by its code's size. Whether Paytm sends packets back to back is not verified live (audit RB-14): the lead decides whether this stays a web defect or the case goes.
The web's LTP frame carries the change the LTP packet has; the desktop's LTP frame carries ltp and the times only.
